# Centered horizontal fibers and LC-positivity

Machine-authored research, request 65c4dfb883e140b0a62fddbffe247137.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains open. No historical novelty is claimed.
Formal validation status is recorded separately in the final validation manifest.

Use the inherited, source-connected horizontal summands

    H(a,j,s,q) = choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q), s>0.

Out-of-range terms are zero. The inherited Lean horizontalTerm uses s-1.
For a fixed combined index k, pair the terms q and k-q in the coefficient of
F_s(t)^2-F_(s-1)(t)F_(s+1)(t). For q<k/2 the signed layer is

    D_q = 2 H_s(q)H_s(k-q)
          -H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(k-q)-H_(s+1)(q)H_(s-1)(k-q).

For 2q=k use H_s(q)^2-H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(q). Retain zeros.
The candidate condition is that every centered tail sum, from r to floor(k/2),
is nonnegative. This is equivalent, by grouping the two convolution orders,
to coefficientwise log-concavity after cutting off every q<r in each F_s.
The exact unsymmetrized convolution identity is formalized in
MarkovTruncatedFiber65c4; the regrouping equivalence in this paragraph is an
elementary paper derivation, not claimed as a separately checked Lean theorem.

This is the LC-positivity framework of Wang--Yeh. Their finite Abel argument
weights signed layers by a nonnegative increasing sequence. For a nonnegative
CrossLC sequence f, the centered products f(q)f(k-q) increase up to the center.
MarkovAbel65c4 checks this finite-sum transfer, including zero weights. Its tail
inequalities remain explicit hypotheses. They are NOT established for all H.
The source transfer from the new truncated-fiber proposition to every Pell
horizontal polygon triple is formalized using the inherited exact bridge.
It still has the truncated-fiber proposition as an unproved premise.

## Exact experiments

pair-probe.json covers all a=3,...,35, 0<=j<=2a, 1<=s<a and
0<=k<=2(a-s). There are 286187 nonzero fibers. All tested centered tails
are nonnegative; after removing zero layers the signs never change from
positive back to negative. At a=3,j=2,s=2,k=2, the layers are [-15,64].
Thus nonnegativity of individual layers is false, while their sum is 49.
The concrete layers and all cutoffs of that fiber are checked in Lean.

pair-random.json records seed 6504, 1500 trials and 703 nonzero fibers with
a<=499, again without a centered-tail or sign-order failure. These are finite
exact experiments and supply no universal statement.

pair-polynomial.json makes a different test. For each s=1,...,8, k=0,...,18
and 0<=j<=2(s+1)+k, replace a by s+k+1+X. Every binomial depending on a is
expanded as its falling-factorial polynomial over Q. This shift puts all
q<=k in the ordinary nonnegative-binomial range. All 19080 centered tails
have nonnegative ordinary X coefficients. This is finite symbolic evidence
for a stronger positivity candidate. It leaves arbitrary s,k and the region
a<s+k+1 unresolved. It is not a proof of universal coefficient positivity.

## A uniform refined fiber

For a=m+3, j=2, center excess s=2 and combined index k=2, write O(m) for
the outer layer and C(m) for the center layer. Direct binomial algebra gives

    2(O(m)+C(m)) = 31m^4+199m^3+435m^2+365m+98.

C(m)>=0 follows from the already proved individual-summand inequality.
Hence both centered tails are nonnegative for every m>=0. For any real
x,z>=0 and xz<=y^2, O(m)xz+C(m)y^2>=0. This is an unbounded parameter
certificate for ONE refined fiber, not for all fibers or the Markov goal.
MarkovFiberPolynomial65c4 checks the identity, positivity and weighted
inequality. It compiled and kernel-replayed successfully; the source hashes
and receipts are in the validation manifest. Its imports reuse inherited
compiled artifacts, rather than a fresh whole-source rebuild.

## Sources and applicability

[Wang--Yeh, Log-concavity and LC-positivity](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0504164v7),
Lemma 2.1 and Section 2, supplies the finite Abel framework and interpretation
of truncated coefficient arrays. Our array also depends on fixed a and j;
their results do not automatically prove its required tail inequalities.

[Chen--Sun, fan coordinates of type A_n](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.09312v1)
treats laminar interval products and the particular exponent map
L(k)=(k1+k2,...,kn+k(n+1)). No identification of this map with the pinned
Markov coefficient fibers was obtained. Its theorem is not imported or applied.

The [published Markov target](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html)
was retrieved live. No source statement is introduced as a Lean axiom.
# Exact Pell sums and a directional pair-fiber conjecture

Machine-authored request 9a720f77696445aab32325da611c5097.
The full pinned Conjecture63 remains unresolved. This report makes no
historical novelty claim. Final formal status is in
evidence/markov-9a720f77/validation.json.

Write a=n+1 for the numerator of the source (n+1)/(n+2), and d=2a.
For every natural i,j with a<=i+j<=2a put r=2a-i-j. The new theorem proves

    A(i,j) = sum over 0<=k<=i and k<=r of
        choose(2a-2r,i-k) choose(a-r+k,k) choose(a-k-1,r-k).

Natural subtraction is used in Lean. Outside the degree strip the expression
is zero. The proof uses literal quotient coefficients and ordinary polynomial
multiplication, and proves the outside-strip zero cases separately. It retains
every raw coefficient and has no denominator cutoff. Together with the prior
diagonal theorem, WeakLC for the entire Pell family is equivalent to the two
horizontal/vertical inequalities for this explicit sum. Both remain unproved.

For positive excess degree i+j=a+s, s>=1, a reindexing gives

    A(i,j) = sum_q H(a,j,s,q),
    H(a,j,s,q) = choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q).

Terms with q>j are zero, as are the out-of-range binomial terms. The formal
horizontalTerm9a72 uses parameter s-1, avoiding negative natural upper indices.
right_horizontal_sum_fixed9a72 proves this identity with the fixed range
0<=q<=a, with all zero terms retained. horizontal_term_lc9a72 proves every
individual summand log-concave as s varies through positive integers. Its proof
uses fixed-upper binomial LC, upper-index binomial LC at stride one and stride
two, and multiplication of nonnegative LC triples. This does not prove the sum
LC; the missing closure is explicitly retained.

## New experimental candidate and its exact formal transfer

Let F_s(t)=sum_q H(a,j,s,q)t^q. The candidate is coefficientwise

    F_(s+1)(t)^2 - F_s(t) F_(s+2)(t) >= 0.

HorizontalFiberGoal9a72 states the corresponding precise bounded-parameter
claim. Evaluating at t=1 would give the raw horizontal inequality.
source_near_one_horizontal_of_fiber9a72 proves that implication for every
actual source path with b=a+1. The j=0 boundary is already proved and is handled
separately. For j>0 the polygon bounds ensure the positive-excess formulas
apply at all three positions. Thus the conditional transfer has no missing
coefficient or zero-support premise. The fiber goal itself is NOT proved.

The complete finite scan through a=50 tested both horizontal and vertical
analogues: 169,050 parameter triples and 2,266,833 nonzero endpoint fibers.
No horizontal failure occurred. The vertical analogue fails at a=10,i=10,
center excess s=1 and combined summand index 16: there are 84 endpoint pairs
but only 81 center pairs. The unrefined raw triple is 1,29,642 and satisfies
the pinned inequality. A further 1,200 deterministic horizontal trials with
a<=250 checked 50,506 nonzero fibers and found no failure. These are finite
experiments, not proofs. Inputs and outputs are saved under evidence/markov-9a720f77/.

There is a potentially useful formal-power-series expression behind H:

    sum_q choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) x^q
      = [z^(a-s)] (1-z)^(-s-1) (1-x*z)^(-s).

This follows by the two negative-binomial expansions. It is a research
derivation, not a new Lean theorem. Combining it with (1+y)^(2s) recovers the
j-refinement. A possible next direction is proving coefficientwise LC through
this generating function or a planar path model; no such proof is asserted.

## Rejected stronger approaches

Termwise midpoint balancing and pairwise synchronization both fail for H.
The exact inequalities are checked in MarkovPellObstructions9a72. Those
failures do not rule out aggregate conservation of the combined index q+r.
The separate vertical decomposition fails even that aggregate condition.

For actual source 3/4, the vertical slice i=3 is [1,8,26,20]. The formal
normalization obstruction is 8^2<3*1*26; the raw inequalities still hold.
Exact rational Sturm experiments on 966 nonzero Pell horizontal/vertical
slices find non-real roots, including this cubic and a horizontal slice at
7/8. The Sturm implementation is experimental evidence, not a Lean theorem.

# Normalized centered layers

Machine-authored request 6a40862beebd4a1a8207ff0222f0451d. The full pinned
Conjecture63 remains unresolved. No novelty claim. Formal acceptance status
is in evidence/markov-6a40862b/validation.json, not inferred from this text.

Use the inherited exact Pell summand

    H_s(q)=choose(a-q,s) choose(s+q-1,q) choose(2s,j-q).

Its center support for s>=2 is the integer interval
max(0,j-2s)<=q<=min(j,a-s). Fix q+r=k. On common center support put

    A(q)=(2s-j+q)(2s-1-j+q)/((a-s-q+1)(s+q-1)),
    B(q)=(a-s-q)(s+q)/((2s+2-j+q)(2s+1-j+q)),
    K=(s-1)(2s+1)/(s(2s-1)).

Elementary binomial ratios give the proposed identification

    [2 H_s(q)H_s(r)-H_(s-1)(q)H_(s+1)(r)
                         -H_(s+1)(q)H_(s-1)(r)]/[H_s(q)H_s(r)]
      = 2-K[A(q)B(r)+A(r)B(q)].

The separate ratios are H_(s-1)(q)/H_s(q)=(s-1)/(2(2s-1))*A(q)
and H_(s+1)(q)/H_s(q)=2(2s+1)/s*B(q). The factors 0 and 1 in
the numerator preserve lower-strip zero cases, and a-s-q=0 preserves the
upper-strip endpoint. No coefficient normalization is proposed for the root:
division here is only for analyzing signed auxiliary layers with positive M.

## Exact rational certificate

Let N(q,r)/D(q,r)=A(q)B(r)+A(r)B(q), using the common denominator

    D(q,r)=AD(q) BD(q) AD(r) BD(r).

The Lean definitions layerAN6, layerAD6, layerBN6, layerBD6, layerN6,
layerD6 record the literal numerators and denominators without cancellation.
For real parameters with q>=0, q+2<=r<=j<=2s+q, a>=s+r, put

    x=q+(j-r)/2, d=r-q-2, e=2s-j+q, h=a-s-r.

These four slacks are nonnegative. Translation by (j-r)/2 leaves all four
linear-factor pairs invariant. In reduced coordinates r=x+d+2,
s=(d+e+2)/2, j=r, a=s+r+h, exact expansion gives

    N(q,r)D(q+1,r-1)-N(q+1,r-1)D(q,r)
       =(d+1)(e+2)(d+e+3) C(x,d,e,h),

where C has 1140 positive rational monomial coefficients. Its complete exact
coefficient list is reduced-certificate.json. It is stored in Lean in Horner
form, grouped by the five powers of x. The identity is split into five
coefficient comparisons to avoid the monolithic elaboration timeout.

When s>1, both D values are strictly positive on the stated domain. Thus the
rational sum A(q)B(r)+A(r)B(q) is nonincreasing as q,r move one step toward
their midpoint. The normalized signed layer is consequently nondecreasing.
The formal rational theorem, if listed as validated, is layer_ratio_monotone6.

## Limits and next bridge

The elementary binomial recurrence identities bc_lower6 and bc_upper6 and
their division corollaries are checked separately. The full identity between
H ratios and the rational functions above has NOT been assembled in Lean.
It is tested exactly in the accompanying finite experiment and derived above,
but is not a checked source theorem. The proof must still handle support

This approach can establish a single sign change from negative to positive

## Unbounded zero-weight result

P_a(0)=D^a. If i+j=a+k, its literal raw coefficient is

    [u^i v^j]P_a(0) = choose(a,k) choose(2k,j).

If i+j<a, the coefficient is zero. This is proved using the exact shear
u=x,v=xy, under which P_a(0)=x^a(1+x(1+y)^2)^a. No coefficient
normalization occurs. Every natural a,i,j is retained, including a=0,
out-of-support positions and internal zeros.

The horizontal inequalities follow by multiplying binomial log-concavity
in k with upper-index-stride-two binomial log-concavity. The diagonals are
ordinary binomial sequences with a constant nonnegative factor.

For the vertical direction put B(a,k,j)=choose(a,k)choose(2k,j). Inside
its support, an exact recurrence is

    B(a,k+1,j+1)(j+1)(2k+1-j)=2(a-k)(2k+1)B(a,k,j).

Write r=2k-j. The numerator controlling the decrease of consecutive ratios is

    =2(a-k-1)((j+1)^2+(r+1)^2-1)
      +2(2k+1)(j+2)(r+2).

It is nonnegative for k+2<=a and j<=2k. Outside these conditions an
endpoint vanishes. The Lean proof clears positive denominators and never
divides by a coefficient. MarkovZeroAll80b7 proves GlobalLC18(P_a(0)),
all three directions at all natural positions. This is a deformation theorem,
not a theorem at source weight one and not a root resolution.

theorem tail_weight_nonneg65c4 (n : ℕ) (a w : ℕ → ℝ)

    (x+y)^(2s) / ((1-x)^(s+1) (1-y)^s).

For an arbitrary word A w B, let n=length(w), m=count_B(w). When w is
nonempty, let f and r indicate that its first and last letters are B, and
let k count adjacent BB pairs inside w. Put s=f+r+2k. The exact formula for
n>=3 is

    2 [v²]P = u^m (1+u)^(n-3) Q(u),
    Q(u) = 4s + (9m²+13m+6)u
         + (6m²+6mn+8m+6n+6)u²
         + (m+n+2)(m+n+1)u³.

There is also a denominator-cleared identity valid for every nonempty core:
multiply the second coefficient by 2(1+u)^3 and the cubic by u^m(1+u)^n.
The formula is proved by a second-order coefficient invariant of the literal
positive matrix recurrence, over arbitrary commutative rings. In particular,
the order-dependent constant is not replaced by a conjectured count formula.
An induction proves 0<=s<=2m.

For actual source words, a=m+1 and b=n+2. If n>2m, the exponent (m,2)
lies below the source polygon. The inherited support theorem therefore makes
its raw coefficient zero. Extracting coefficient m from the displayed formula
forces s=0. This uses an actual source theorem, not an assumed balanced-word
identification. If n<=2m, the elementary bound s<=2m suffices instead.

Write the cubic coefficients as A,B,C,D. The polynomial certificates establish
A,C,B,D>=0, AC<=B², BD<=C² and AD<=BC for m<=n and
(n<=2m or s=0). They yield the zero-extended CrossLC property of Q. The already
checked binomial smoothing and shift adapters yield CrossLC of the literal
source row. Seven core words of length at most two are evaluated separately;
their rows are shifted nonnegative quadratics with checked coefficient gaps.

research/MarkovSecondHorizontal8934.lean. Consult the validation manifest for
actual accepted build/replay status, rather than treating this prose as a receipt.

This argument does not establish the stronger arbitrary-word horizontal
conjecture. The cubic before binomial smoothing can fail LC for long words
with B at a core endpoint, so merely applying residual LC to every word would

matrix-invariants.json records 1,023 products beginning with A through length

# Independent audit of the Markov core, log-concavity, and boundary modules

Markov.lean, MarkovLogConcavity.lean, MarkovBoundary.lean, MarkovExamples.lean,
and MarkovIndices.lean were copied and compiled independently against the pinned
dependencies. The four unchanged modules retain their previously verified builds;
the new Indices module was independently compiled here. All 48 named theorems
have only propext, Classical.choice, and
Quot.sound in their axiom closures. Exact snapshots, hashes, compilation output,
and axiom output are recorded in report.json. No active source was edited and
no mathematical proof hint was supplied to the proposer.

## Family and target definitions

BiPoly is a polynomial in u with integer-polynomial coefficients in v.
The coefficient function therefore returns the ordinary integer coefficient
of u^i v^j. The seeds and both recurrence orientations match the source
numerator recurrence specialized at w=1. The previous independent scan audit
separately verified the exact original Laurent mutation on its finite family.

InPolygon is the stated polygon in natural indices, with nonnegativity supplied
by their type. WeakLC covers every consecutive horizontal, vertical, and
constant-i+j triple without subtracting natural indices or omitting zeros.
Conjecture63 is explicitly a proposition definition, not a theorem. It contains
both endpoints and all finite generated middle labels. The 0/1 polygon reduces
to its singleton and the 1/1 polygon has only two lattice points, as intended.
General path/fraction completeness and recurrence/source identification are
not silently proved by these definitions.

## Strong sequence invariant and smoothing

CrossLC demands all cross inequalities f(i)f(j+1)<=f(i+1)f(j) for i<=j.
It is stronger than merely adjacent log-concavity for an arbitrary sequence.
The file does not assume that arbitrary adjacent inequalities imply CrossLC.
Instead it proves CrossLC for the nonnegative three-term seed under AC<=B^2.

The shift and forward-sum proofs preserve CrossLC. For distinct integer
indices, the proof uses the four appropriate cross inequalities, including
i+1<=j; the equal-index case is equality. There is no unjustified division by
coefficients and no suppressed positivity assumption. The resulting Smooth
operator f(k)+f(k-1), and any finite Pascal iteration, preserve CrossLC.
The adjacent conclusion then follows by the explicit specialization i=k-1,
j=k. Zero coefficients remain present throughout.

## Exact ordinary-polynomial coefficient bridge

CoeffSeq first tests whether its integer index is negative and returns zero
there. Only nonnegative indices are converted to natural indices. Ordinary
polynomial coefficients also vanish past the degree. This is the correct
zero extension, not an accidental truncation of negative indices to zero.

coeffSeq_smooth, coeffSeq_quadratic, and coeffSeq_binomial_mul identify the
abstract sequence with the actual coefficients of (1+X)^n times the stated
quadratic. Consequently quadratic_binomial_logConcave proves an ordinary raw
coefficient inequality, not a factorial-normalized substitute. Its assumptions
are A,B,C>=0 and AC<=B^2; no real-rootedness assertion is made or needed.

## Universal third-diagonal expression theorem

ThirdA=(a-1)(a-2)/2, ThirdB=ab-4a+2, and ThirdC=(b-1)(b-2)/2
are exactly the coefficients in the published factored third-diagonal
expression. third_gap_certificate is a checked exact polynomial identity.
third_parameters derives nonnegativity and the quadratic coefficient
inequality for real a>=3 and b>=a+1 by that identity and nonnegative terms.

third_diagonal_expression_logConcave therefore proves, for every pair of
natural numbers 3<=a<b and every integer k, the adjacent coefficient inequality
for

    (1+X)^(a+b-5) * (ThirdA a + ThirdB a b*X + ThirdC b*X^2).

The exponent is in its ordinary-polynomial range under these hypotheses;
natural subtraction causes no negative-exponent truncation. No gcd or ratio
restriction is necessary for this explicit-polynomial theorem. It does not
cover the a=1 and a=2 families. It proves at least weak log-concavity and does
not assert real-rootedness or a full two-dimensional inequality.

## Scope conclusion

No mathematical error or statement mismatch was found. The two important
bridges must remain distinct: the polynomial-to-Pascal coefficient bridge is
proved here; the recurrence-generated Markov numerator-to-third-diagonal
expression bridge remains a separate formal obligation. The theorem's own
comment states that restriction correctly. Full Conjecture 6.3 remains open.

The boundary result, added third-diagonal transfer, and completed examples
are covered below.


## Added third-diagonal expression and transfer

SourceThird gives the source's literal three-term polynomial expression, with
parameter n=a+b-5. sourceThird_factor proves that it equals the quadratic-times-
binomial form previously audited. DiagonalSeq extends the actual raw diagonal
coefficient list by zero outside 0<=k<=d; it tests those bounds before natural
subtraction, so negative indices do not collapse onto coefficient zero.

ThirdDiagonalFormula is a proposition definition asserting equality of the
actual diagonal sequence and the source expression. It is not an axiom or an
established universal identity. third_diagonal_of_formula derives the raw
inequality from this explicit hypothesis for 3<=a<b. The new code therefore
exposes the remaining identification obligation instead of silently treating
it as discharged. All exponents are in their ordinary-polynomial range under
the transfer theorem's hypotheses.

## Fully connected j=0 boundary result

edgeEval sets the inner polynomial variable v to zero and casts integer
coefficients to real coefficients. The new theorem edgeEval_coeff explicitly
proves that its ith coefficient is the real cast of coeff P i 0. Thus no
coefficient specialization, orientation, or normalization bridge is missing.

EdgeFormula records both denominator-label positivity and the equality
edgeEval P = X^a (X+1)^(b-1). Its initial cases are proved. Its recurrence step
uses positive b to kill the V^b subtraction term at v=0 and correctly combines
the remaining exponents. Induction covers every finite left/right path of the
actual defined recurrence. No finite denominator bound is used and no boundary
coefficient identity is taken as an external assumption.

The coefficient sequence of X^a(1+X)^n is proved CrossLC using the audited
smoothing and shift lemmas. boundary_logConcave applies this to the generated
boundary, and boundary_raw_logConcave transports it to the literal integer
raw coefficients used by WeakLC:

    A(i,0) A(i+2,0) <= A(i+1,0)^2

for every natural i and every finite path. This is stronger than restricting
to polygon triples along that boundary. Positivity of label denominators makes
the natural exponent b-1 legitimate. No truncated-index artifact is used.

This is an unconditional universal theorem for the generated j=0 boundary.
It re-establishes a known boundary result in the source; it is not a solution
of all interior lines or all directions of Conjecture 6.3. No mathematical
error or misleading scope claim was found in the accepted modules.


## Completed examples and missing-condition distinctions

The left child is explicitly expanded as the 1/3 numerator. Its raw vertical
coefficients at (1,0),(1,1),(1,2) are proved equal to 1,2,3. The corresponding
raw inequality is strictly satisfied, and division by the correct multinomial
factors 3,6,3 gives a strictly reversed inequality. Thus the normalized failure
belongs to the actual generated family and does not refute its raw target.

Both three-term sequences [1,2,1] and [0,2,0] satisfy CrossLC, while their
nonnegative difference [1,0,1] fails. This correctly disproves unrestricted
subtraction preservation. It does not disprove the specific Markov recurrence.

The parameter pair (3,4) gives the seed 1+2X+3X^2. Both the negative
quadratic discriminant and its coefficient inequality are proved; the separate
strict-positivity theorem at every real x confirms there is no real root.
This rules out a real-rootedness requirement for the present coefficient result,
without ruling out coefficient log-concavity.

The two endpoint WeakLC assertions are vacuous because no three-point line fits
inside their polygons. At the initial 1/2 label the only relevant three-point
line has coefficients [1,2,1]; the code correctly proves that case while the
other directions are vacuous. No support positions are silently removed.

All accepted example statements match these interpretations. The final six
index theorems are additionally audited below.


## Final index invariant and reduced-label theorem

FrameIndices records that the middle is the mediant of the two endpoints,
the oriented determinant is one, the endpoint denominators are positive,
the upper endpoint has positive numerator, and the endpoints lie within the
stated bounds of [0,1]. These are true initially and are proved preserved by
both actual recurrence branches; fold induction covers every finite path.

coprime_of_det correctly derives coprimality from c*b=a*d+1: the gcd of a,b
divides both products, hence divides 1. frame_reduced applies this to the
middle and upper labels. Its exact conclusion is 0<a<b and gcd(a,b)=1 for
every generated middle label. This is a soundness-of-labeling theorem. It
asserts neither injectivity of path labeling nor surjectivity onto all reduced
fractions. The new documentation explicitly retains general coverage as a
formal obligation. No circular assumption about coverage or log-concavity
enters the invariant proof.

Final mathematical source hashes all agree with the independently checked
snapshots. Documentation equivalence is reviewed in DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md.
No error or misleading mathematical scope claim was found in the final
accepted five-module, 48-theorem construction.
